tags.name: Alex's Cave Dive Site
tags.description: Cave carved by the waves into the islet between Comino and Cominotto, with a sandy floor and smooth walls. In calm weather you can see daylight through a chimney at the back. With enough air you can continue through a tunnel to Crystal Lagoon. Usually dived after Lantern Point West.
tags.dive:conditions: Dangerous in a southerly storm, otherwise sheltered.

tags.name: Anchor Bay (Dive Site)
tags.description: Small bay below Popeye Village near Mellieħa. Shore dive from the jetty to a large anchor, a varied reef, a shallow training area and Scorpion Cave on the south side. Popular for training and first dives.
tags.dive:conditions: One of the few sites still diveable in strong north-easterly winds.

tags.name: Anchor Reef (Dive Site)
tags.description: Wall along the south side of Cominotto, 15–25 m at the top with overhangs and ledges. At about 35 m there's an old anchor with four flukes.
tags.dive:conditions: Exposed to north-westerly winds.

tags.name: Balluta Bay (Dive Site)
tags.description: Shallow bay in St Julian's: rocky reef with sand and seagrass down to about 12 m. Octopus and cuttlefish are common, and there are sometimes seahorses in the seagrass. A popular night dive.
tags.dive:conditions: Currents can be tricky; best in calm weather.

tags.name: Big Bear-Little Bear
tags.description: Two rocks (Big Bear and Little Bear) about 30 m off the Dwejra coast; the site is also called Skuljetti or Rogers Cave. From about 5 m a drop-off leads to Rogers Cave right below the rocks, its walls covered in small corals and sponges, often with slipper lobsters. Boulders with groupers around the bigger rock.

tags.name: Billinghurst Cave
tags.description: Large cave west of Reqqa Point. The entrance is at about 28 m and rises to about 14 m inside. Two big chambers reach about 150 m into the rock; the inner one has an air pocket, but the air is not breathable. Take plenty of air.
tags.dive:level: Experienced (Advanced Open Water and deep experience)
tags.dive:conditions: Only in flat calm conditions; sharp rocks at the entry.

tags.name: Blue Lagoon Tunnel Dive Site
tags.description: Small bay north of the Blue Lagoon, full of friendly bream. A cave on the bay's right leads through the rock point and out to open water. Halfway along, a rock pool lets you come up to open air.
tags.dive:conditions: Sheltered, but very busy with tourist boats in summer.

tags.name: Bottleneck Cave (Dive Site)
tags.description: Deep cave close to Reqqa Point in northern Gozo, along the same coast as Billinghurst Cave. A technical dive.

tags.name: Calypso Cave
tags.description: Cave and arches off the Xwejni–Qbajjar coast near Marsalforn, also called Calypso Tunnel or Triple Arch, in the same area as Double Arch. Not the Calypso Cave on land above Ramla Bay.

tags.name: Cirkewwa - Left Arch (Dive Site)
tags.description: Part of the Paradise Bay reef at Ċirkewwa: boulder fields, sand and seagrass, drop-offs and swim-throughs. The White Arch is a smaller natural arch at about 11 m that reaches almost to the surface.

tags.name: Cirkewwa - Outer Reef (Dive Site)
tags.description: The Ċirkewwa reef continuing north past the tug Rozi and the Arch. The top stays at 15–20 m. About 10 minutes past the Arch the wall gets steeper and drops beyond 40 m.

tags.name: Cirkewwa - Right Arch (Dive Site)
tags.description: Ċirkewwa's best-known feature: a natural arch, really a cavern whose roof collapsed, with its top at 12 m and 8 m above the seabed. Caves and tunnels on the way; easily combined with the tug Rozi.

tags.name: Cirkewwa - Susie's Pool and Reef (Dive Site)
tags.description: Shallow rocky plateau at about 6 m, used for skills practice, next to a reef that drops to about 30 m. The Madonna statue sits in a small cave on the reef wall at 18 m.

tags.name: Cominotto Arch (Dive Site)
tags.description: At Cominotto's south-west tip: a vertical wall to about 39 m with huge boulders forming swim-throughs and caverns, with golden cup corals, chromis and groupers deeper down.
tags.dive:conditions: Exposed with strong currents: experienced divers only.

tags.name: Crystal Lagoon Dive Site
tags.description: Lagoon beside the Blue Lagoon on Comino's west side. Reachable underwater through a tunnel from Alex's Cave.

tags.name: Double Arch Reef
tags.description: Two natural arches, one stacked above the other, about 200 m off Xwejni Bay. The reef top is at 15–18 m, the arches start at 20 m, it's 34 m under the arches and the reef ends at about 45 m. Barracuda shoals are common. Can be done from shore with a long surface swim.
tags.dive:conditions: Best in flat calm; easterly winds blow it out.

tags.name: Fessej Rock
tags.description: Free-standing rock off the mouth of Mġarr ix-Xini, rising from about 50 m to 15 m. Usually dived by circling the rock; large groupers and bream on the deep side.
tags.dive:conditions: Currents and swell can be strong here; a good choice when the wind is north-westerly.

tags.name: Filfla (Dive Site)
tags.description: Uninhabited islet south of Malta, used for target practice until the 1970s and now a nature reserve. Walls go past 70 m. Unexploded munitions lie around the island: keep away from them.
tags.dive:conditions: Diving needs a permit and a licensed boat. Strong currents at times.

tags.name: Filflette (Dive Site)
tags.description: Filfoletta, the rock next to Filfla. Filfla and the sea around it are a nature reserve with unexploded munitions on the seabed.
tags.dive:conditions: Diving needs a permit and a licensed boat.

tags.name: Ghar Lapsi - Finger Reef (Dive Site)
tags.description: Finger-shaped reef at Għar Lapsi with a small colourful wall and a cave you can leave through an opening in its ceiling.
tags.dive:conditions: Currents are common.

tags.name: Għar il-Katidral
tags.description: Cathedral Cave (Blue Dome) near Wied il-Għasri, on the stretch from Forna Point to Reqqa Point. The entrance starts at 5 m; inside you surface in a huge dome lit blue by the light coming through the water. Outside, depths reach 30 m.
tags.dive:conditions: Sheltered inlet. Best between 10:00 and noon. Reaching it from land means a tough scramble down the rocks.

tags.name: diving site Għar Lapsi
tags.description: Small sheltered cove on the south coast of Malta, one of the few shore entries there. Known for a shallow, sunlit cave system over 40 m long with many openings. Reefs (Finger Reef, Middle Reef, Black John) and an underwater nativity crib at 22 m are nearby.
tags.dive:conditions: Steep steps down to the water; currents are common offshore.

tags.name: Għar ta' Ras il-Qamħ
tags.description: Cave and reef at Ras il-Kanun (Ta' Lenk) in northern Gozo, near Cathedral Cave.

British WWII destroyer sunk in Grand Harbour in 1942; its front part was later scuttled in St. Elmo Bay off Valletta. About 42 m of fairly broken wreck on sand at up to 16 m: a real war wreck that beginners can dive from the shore.
tags.name: HMS Maori
Il-Bajja tax-Xwejni
tags.description: Bay west of Marsalforn and the entry point for several sites: the shallow reef, the Washing Machine, Double Arch, Calypso Cave and Submarine Cave.

tags.name: Il-Ħofra tal-Bidwin
tags.description: Blue Hole: a natural sinkhole in the rock at Dwejra, about 15 m deep and sheltered from the sea. An underwater window at about 9 m leads to the open sea, and a big cave lies on the far side. Often combined with Coral Gardens, the Azure Window reef or the Inland Sea.
tags.dive:conditions: 200 m walk over rough rock with all gear. Good in the afternoon when other sites get rough.

tags.name: Inland Sea
tags.description: Dive site in the Dwejra Inland Sea (Qawra tad-Dwejra). The lagoon itself is about 2 m deep. An 80 m tunnel through the cliff leads to the open sea, from 3 m on the lagoon side to 26 m at the seaward end; outside, the seabed keeps dropping past 40 m.
tags.dive:conditions: Watch out for the tourist boats that use the tunnel.

tags.name: Kristu I-Bahhar (dive Site)
tags.description: Kristu l-Baħħar: a 3 m statue of Christ standing on white sand at about 35 m off Qawra Point. First placed off St. Paul's Island in 1990, then relocated in 2000, next to the wreck of MV Imperial Eagle.
tags.dive:level: Experienced (Advanced Open Water and deep experience)

tags.name: L-Ahair Point (Dive Site)
tags.description: Long reef off L-Aħrax Point at the northern tip of Malta: rocks, little canyons, passages to swim through and seagrass. It's a long way from where you get in, so a boat is often used.

tags.name: L-Aħrax (Dive Site)
tags.description: Northern tip of Malta with several shore dives: a small cave at the point, the North Reef, a tunnel open to the surface into a small inland sea, and a cavern known as the Inland Sea or Coral Lagoon.

tags.name: Lantern Point Dive Site
tags.description: South-west tip of Comino by the lighthouse. A chimney drops from a plateau at about 6 m and comes out at 16 m; below it a wall with huge boulders, caverns and swim-throughs goes past 50 m.
tags.dive:conditions: Very exposed: dive only in perfect weather.

tags.name: Lantern Point West Dive Site
tags.description: Just north of the lighthouse on Comino: a vertical wall into large boulders and seagrass, and a shallow cave where the rock is split by a vertical crack.
tags.dive:conditions: Sheltered from south-easterly winds, but surge and current are possible.

tags.name: Madonna Statue (Dive Site)
tags.description: A Madonna statue set in a small cave halfway along the Susie's Pool reef wall, at 18 m. Placed by the Amphibians Diving Club in 1987.

tags.name: Mini Blue Hole (Dive Site)
tags.description: Small hole in the rock near Żonqor Point, Marsaskala, connected to the sea by a 10 m tunnel whose entrance is a few metres from the entry, at 7 m. The hole itself is only 3 m deep; beautiful light for photos.

tags.name: MT Hephaestus
tags.note: Scuttled 2022-08 as an attraction for scuba divers
tags.description: Oil tanker, about 60 m long, that ran aground at Qawra Point in a storm in 2018 and was scuttled off Xatt l-Aħmar in August 2022 as a dive site.
tags.dive:level: Experienced (Advanced Open Water and deep experience)

tags.name: MV Cominoland
tags.description: Former Captain Morgan cruise boat, about 35 m long, scuttled in 2006. Sits upright on sand at about 40 m; two decks that are safe to enter through openings cut before sinking.
tags.dive:level: Experienced (Advanced Open Water and deep experience)

tags.name: MV Karwela
tags.description: Former Captain Morgan harbour ferry, about 50 m long, scuttled in 2006. Upright on sand with its bow at 39 m and stern at 41 m; the upper deck begins at 30 m. Prepared for safe penetration.
tags.dive:level: Experienced (Advanced Open Water and deep experience)

tags.name: MV Xlendi
tags.description: Former Gozo Channel ferry, about 80 m long, scuttled in 1999. It lies upside down at 42–44 m with the propellers at about 32 m. Don't go inside: the wreck is unstable.
tags.dive:level: Experienced (Advanced Open Water and deep experience)

tags.name: Mġarr ix-Xini
tags.description: Narrow inlet on the south coast of Gozo. Easy shore dive along the right-hand cliff to a large cave near the mouth of the bay, then back over the sandy bottom.
tags.dive:conditions: Still diveable when the wind is north-westerly, which few sites are; popular with swimmers.

tags.name: P31 - Patrol Boat
tags.description: Former Armed Forces of Malta patrol boat, 52 m long, scuttled in 2009 off the west coast of Comino. Rests nearly level on white sand at about 20 m with its top at 7 m; a good training wreck.

tags.name: Qawra North (Dive Site)
tags.description: Reef north of Qawra Point: the seabed slopes to 10 m, then a small wall to sand at 15 m. Near the west end a small arch at 18 m is big enough to swim through.

tags.name: Qawra South (Dive Site)
tags.description: Protected bay on the south-eastern flank of Qawra Point, 2–10 m deep over sand and seagrass. Used for training and try dives.

tags.name: Qbajjar Reef
tags.description: Shallow reef along the Xwejni–Qbajjar coast west of Marsalforn.

tags.name: Ras il-Ħobż (Dive Site)
tags.description: Middle Finger: a pinnacle rising from 40+ m to about 10 m, with amberjack, dentex and moray eels. The slope keeps going past 80 m, so it's used for technical training from the shore; the best parts are within 25 m.
Northernmost point of Gozo: a wall with excellent visibility and large groupers, dropping past 70 m. Billinghurst Cave is about 150 m left of where you get in.
tags.name: Reqqa Point
tags.dive:conditions: Hard to get in and out when the sea is choppy; sharp rocks.

tags.name: Santa Marija Caves Dive Site
tags.description: Connected caves and tunnels in an inlet near Santa Marija Bay on Comino, 8–12 m deep. Bream swarm around divers here. Safe and fun for less experienced divers.
tags.dive:conditions: Sheltered from north-westerly winds.

tags.name: Santa Marija Point
tags.description: Probably the Santa Maria breakwater at Marsalforn: a gently sloping, shallow site (6–10 m) mainly used for training.

tags.name: Santa Marija Reef Dive Site
tags.description: Low rocky reef off the northern point of Comino with gullies, caverns and swim-throughs; schools of bream, salema and mullet.
tags.dive:conditions: Getting back on the boat can be hard in chop and swell.

tags.name: Scorpion Cave (Dive Site)
tags.description: Large shallow cavern on the south side of Anchor Bay, about 150 m from the jetty. The entrance is behind a large boulder in 6 to 10 m of water; inside there's a big dome where you can come up into air.

tags.name: Sirens (Dive Site)
tags.description: Shallow reef by the Sirens quay in St. Paul's Bay, down to 12 m: rocks, sand and seagrass with octopus, moray eels and cuttlefish. Mostly used for training and try dives.

tags.name: St. Elmo - Left Reef (Dive Site)
tags.description: Reef below Fort St. Elmo at the tip of Valletta, starting at about 13 m and dropping off to 35 m. Boulders and gullies with moray eels, octopus and groupers; HMS Maori is next door.

tags.name: St. Elmo - Right Reef (Dive Site)
tags.description: Reef below Fort St. Elmo at the tip of Valletta, starting at about 13 m and dropping off to 35 m. Boulders and gullies with moray eels, octopus and groupers.

tags.name: Stork Rock (Dive Site)
tags.description: Near Filfla. Filfla and the sea around it are a nature reserve with unexploded munitions on the seabed.
tags.dive:conditions: Diving needs a permit and a licensed boat.

tags.name: Dive Site and Shipwreck
tags.description: Sultan Rock at the south-east point of Comino: big boulders covered in algae, seagrass with wrasse, moray eels and groupers, and scattered remains of the wreck of HMS Sultan. Not deep, but the currents make it a dive for experienced divers.
tags.dive:conditions: Protected from north-westerlies, but the surface can get rough and currents are strong.

tags.name: Ta' Ċenċ Dive Site
tags.description: Wall dive near Mġarr ix-Xini: from the canyon over boulders to a steep sloping wall. On the way back there's a cave at 14 m that goes far in.
tags.dive:conditions: Sheltered from north-westerly winds.

tags.name: The Washing Machine
tags.description: Shallow site off Xwejni Bay near Marsalforn.

tags.name: Tug 2 Reef (Dive Site)
tags.description: Former Grand Harbour tug, 30 m long, scuttled off Exiles in Sliema in 2013. Lies at about 22 m, roughly 250 m from the entry; a storm in 2016 pushed it bow-first into the reef. Open and safe to swim through.
Libyan tanker, about 110 m long, scuttled off Wied iż-Żurrieq in 1998 after a fatal explosion in dry dock. Sits upright on sand at 36 m; widely seen as Malta's best wreck dive.
tags.name: Um El Faroud
tags.source: Maltese Islands Diving Guide, =BjP= (SSI Instructor Trainer)

tags.name: Wreck of SS Margit
tags.description: Passenger steamship bombed and sunk in Kalkara Creek in April 1941. Lies broken on a silty bottom at about 22 m. Visibility is lower than elsewhere because it's in the harbour.

tags.name: Xatt l-Aħmar Reef
tags.description: Reef along the south side of Xatt l-Aħmar bay, from the same entry as the three wrecks. A long snorkel out leads to a drop-off with boulders, nooks and crannies, small groupers, octopus and bream.
tags.dive:conditions: A good option when a north-westerly wind closes other sites. A 4x4 helps on the dirt track.

tags.name: Xlendi Tunnel
tags.description: Shallow tunnel, about 70 m long, through the headland on the north side of Xlendi Bay. The entrance is at 5 m and it's 8 m at the deepest. You can surface in many places, so it suits less experienced divers.
tags.dive:conditions: Watch out for boats in the bay.

tags.name: Zurrieq - Left Reef (Dive Site)
tags.description: Wall reef on the east side of Wied iż-Żurrieq, going past 30 m, with good visibility and shoals of small fish.

tags.name: Zurrieq - Right Reef (Dive Site)
tags.description: Reef on the west side of Wied iż-Żurrieq with drop-offs, gullies and two caves: Bell Tower Cave (three entrances, the deepest at 27 m) and Mouse Hole Cave (25 m). A diving-helmet statue sits on the sand at about 28 m.

tags.name: Zurrieq - Valley (Dive Site)
tags.description: The narrow inlet where all Wied iż-Żurrieq shore dives start, sloping gently to about 15 m. Used for training and night dives; from here you reach East Reef, West Reef and the Um El Faroud.
Sandy bay on the south-east coast of Gozo facing Comino, 5–12 m deep. Good for courses and introductory dives.
tags.name: Ħondoq ir-Rummien
